input: Scheduled ventures brief: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products (full text in prompts/ventures/prompt-1.md)

doc_friction.issue: 'Start here' named open-tennis-robots (a CAD survey-drill item); ifc-quantity-takeoff (2 commits in 7 days, a clear buildable item) was row 9. The draw ignores how much buildable work a row has left.

Its open-PR column showed no claim on ifc-quantity-takeoff at 23:56; #17823 opened a minute later. This session only saw the claim when allocate.py --venture ran an hour in, after the work was built. Claiming first (as the output says) would have caught it; I skipped that step.

deviations.why: Took flagship row 9 (ifc-quantity-takeoff, faceted-body sections) instead of the 'Start here' row (open-tennis-robots). The last session sent there left it too, and its buildable item is a marginal survey drill.
deviations.did: Built plane sections of meshes and measured them on 8 public models
deviations.result: 4,251 more stored areas checked, 2,915 agree; merged

deviations.why: Draft PR #17823 (empty claim commit) claimed the same item 7 minutes after this session started. By the time I saw it, the implementation, tests and eval here were finished, so yielding would have thrown away finished work while the other session had pushed nothing.
deviations.did: Landed this PR; its body names #17823 so the other session's claim_check sees LANDED

deviations.why: Did not open a draft PR before building (skipped the claim step), which is what caused the overlap above.

notes: Verification: node --test in the venture (32 pass); run_venture_tests.py ifc-quantity-takeoff ok; seeded faults (exit/entry swap in shellSection, brep void sign) each fail a test; stored-vs-computed volume output identical to the 2026-11-19 file on all 13 models (apart from timings); check_posts ok; venture-preflight run (see PR).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a geometry engineer implementing mesh plane sections, tests, and a corpus eval of 8 models

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
